messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: VaultCore (vc-451) private VPC — NLB healthchecks failing on inbound NLB (10:05 UTC). Multiple target healths UNHEALTHY, customer-facing 502/504. Pager: oncall-network.

maya-ops: Ack, joining. Pulling target-group and NLB logs.

pranav-net: I see healthcheck 502 from targets -> backend returning 504 at the app layer. Connection resets in ELB logs.

sam-infra: Quick check: NAT instance conntrack counters spiking for vc-451 tenant. If conntrack exhausted, new connections reset -> 5xx.

amy-cs: Talking to VaultCore SRE now. They confirm spike started ~10:04 UTC after a batch import job. Customer impact: inference calls intermittently failing, roughly 60-75% error rate.

pranav-net: Running target health describe:

```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/vc-451-inbound
# shows many targets Unhealthy (FailedHealthChecks)
```

sam-infra: Checking conntrack:

```
# on NAT instance: 
sudo conntrack -S | grep entries
# output: entries=195200 (limit 196608)
```

sam-infra: Conntrack nearly full. Increasing nf_conntrack_max to 262144 while we triage.

```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
# echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
```

maya-ops: Applying now on NATs in us-east-1-private.

opsbot: runbook step executed: increased conntrack on nat-1, nat-2.

pranav-net: I see immediate drop in reset rate on NLB logs, a few targets recovering health. Still seeing some 502s from backend timeouts.

kyle-security: Security check — no SG changes made. NAT still in place. If we need to scale NATs, will open change with Ops.

amy-cs: Customer SRE reports partial recovery, errors down to ~25% now. They're going to throttle their import job and backfill.

sam-infra: To prevent recurrence, we should:
- scale NAT capacity (add additional NAT instances)
- enable connection tracking tuning persistently via cloud-init
- consider NAT Gateway for heavier tenants (VaultCore is high-variance)

pranav-net: Short-term failover option: shift inbound traffic for vc-451 to the ALB fallback pool (ALB is in same VPC) to avoid NAT path for specific control-plane calls. I can change target-group weight to 0/100 for NLB -> ALB path. Need CS approval.

amy-cs: Customer approved ALB fallback for control plane only. They don't want inference traffic moved yet. Proceed with limited shift.

pranav-net: Executing weighted shift:

```
# change route weight in our router service
routerctl set-weight vc-451 inbound nlb=10 alb=90 --dry-run
routerctl set-weight vc-451 inbound nlb=10 alb=90
```

opsbot: routerctl: weight change applied for vc-451 inbound.

pranav-net: Healthchecks recovering across the board, backend latency reduced. Monitoring for 10m.

maya-ops: Noting mitigation steps in incident ticket INC-2026-451. Adding timeline and commands.

sam-infra: I'll spin up two extra NAT instances and attach them to the tenant routing table. Commands:

```
# launch via autoscale group override
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name vc-451-nat-asg --desired-capacity 4
```

sam-infra: NATs up and seen in route table. Conntrack dips to 60k used.

amy-cs: Customer confirms normalizing traffic from their side. They will re-run import slowly and report.

kyle-security: Recommend we add a security note to the postmortem: tenant batch jobs can exhaust conntrack. Consider quota/circuit-breaker for future.

maya-ops: Agreed. I'll create action items: persistent conntrack config, NAT autoscale policy improvements, playbook update to prefer ALB fallback for heavy-control operations.

erin-oncall: Erin taking over primary for monitoring and follow-up. Handing off at 11:00 UTC. All clear on my side to keep watch.

maya-ops: Thanks Erin. Transitioned.

incident-bot: STATUS: Mitigation applied at 10:27 UTC — conntrack increased, additional NATs launched, selective inbound routed to ALB. Healthchecks recovered to 99.6% success over last 5m. Customer impact reduced to <1% errors.

pranav-net: Leaving temp ALB fallback in place for 1 hour, then gradual rollback to NLB once stable.

amy-cs: Customer thanked the team, will wait for postmortem and longer-term changes.

opsbot: Next steps assigned: Maya-ops (postmortem + playbook), Sam-infra (persistent sysctl + autoscale), Kyle-security (quota/circuit-breaker proposal).

erin-oncall: Monitoring. Logging a note in the oncall handoff doc. If errors creep back, escalate to paging.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: Resolved (mitigated) at 10:40 UTC. Monitoring window started.
